title: PSCD-GS: Role-Aware Perception-Structure Collaborative Densification for 3D Gaussian Splatting
abstract: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) enables efficient, high-quality novel-view synthesis, but its reconstruction quality remains sensitive to how Gaussian primitives are densified during optimization. Existing densification strategies commonly rely on gradients, reconstruction errors, or isolated regional cues, which may not capture the complementary perceptual and structural characteristics of a scene. We propose PSCD-GS, a role-aware perception-structure collaborative densification framework that integrates image-space perceptual responses with multi-view structural evidence. These cues are projected onto individual Gaussian primitives through rendering-contribution-weighted aggregation, producing continuous memberships for perception-dominant, structure-dominant, co-dominant, and low-response behaviors. This primitive-level representation is used to prioritize densification candidates, select between cloning and splitting, and guide the placement of newly generated Gaussians. Experiments on Mip-NeRF 360, Deep Blending, and Tanks & Temples show that PSCD-GS achieves competitive dataset-level rendering quality while maintaining a controlled Gaussian representation. Qualitative comparisons suggest better preservation of fine textures, object boundaries, and thin structures. These results indicate that jointly modeling perceptual and structural evidence can provide more informative guidance for selective Gaussian densification.
